definitions: To enter a place rudely or abruptly, often interrupting something.
To collide with someone or something in a clumsy or forceful way.
examples: He tends to barge into conversations without an invitation.
She barged into the room, demanding an explanation.
I didn't mean to barge into you, I wasn't looking where I was going.
pastTenses: barged into (past simple), barged into (past perfect)
